learningObjectives: Link TestSheet Instances to Requirements by drag-and-drop.
Explain the difference between a TestCase-Substitute link and a TestCase link.
Explain how ExecutionLists connect to RequirementSets to build a project dashboard.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Why link TestCase Design back to Requirements

elements.description: Requirement links distinguish planned design data from physical TestCases and execution evidence. A TestSheet or selected Instances can establish planned coverage before executable tests exist; this is not proof that the application was tested successfully.

Drag Instances from the TestSheet onto their matching Requirement. If every Instance on the TestSheet belongs to that Requirement, the whole TestSheet can be dragged at once. If only some Instances are in scope right now — for example, only the ones planned for the current sprint — select and drag just those individual Instances instead.
Linking TestSheet, Class or Instance data creates a substitute for each linked Instance. A substitute represents planned test data, not an executed or passed test.

Creating a physical TestCase does not by itself replace its substitute. Drag the TestCase onto the corresponding substitute link. Alternatively, use Replace Substitutes by Testcases on the RequirementSet; the required TestCases must be used in an ExecutionList and that ExecutionList must be linked to the RequirementSet.

bulletPoints: Drag the whole TestSheet when all its Instances belong to one Requirement; drag individual Instances when only a subset does (e.g. this sprint's data).
Replace substitutes explicitly; keep the source Instance, physical TestCase and execution links aligned.

elements.description: The documentation recommends TestSheet coverage for application Requirements. Choose a structure that keeps each Requirement traceable; the same Requirement can receive selected Instances or Class data. One TestSheet per Requirement is a useful organizational choice, not a prohibition on other documented link scopes.

elements.term: Link an ExecutionList to a RequirementSet
elements.description: Drag an ExecutionList onto a RequirementSet to create its link. Merely creating the list does not establish this relationship. An ExecutionEntry can separately be dragged onto an individual Requirement to create a TestCase link. Its LinkExecutionEntryHandleExecutionList setting controls whether the associated ExecutionList is added to the set: AlwaysAdd, AskUser or NeverAdd.

elements.text: The dashboard also needs current calculations. AutoCalculateRequirements is off by default. Use Update Outdated Values on a RequirementSet (or the Requirements menu for all sets), or enable automatic calculation in Commander > General > Advanced and restart Tosca. A blue exclamation mark indicates outdated values.

bulletPoints: ExecutionList → RequirementSet and ExecutionEntry → individual Requirement are distinct operations.
Inspect TestCase and execution evidence separately from planned coverage; recalculate outdated values.

elements.text: Independent Quilyn exercise: link only the Instances in scope, inspect their substitutes, create physical tests and replace the substitutes explicitly, then link the ExecutionList to the set and recalculate. The original Academy video and exercise files require access and have not been verified here.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing TestCase-Substitute links with TestCase links
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming both terms describe the same thing at different points in the process.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: A substitute is planned data. Replace it by dragging the physical TestCase onto it or by the documented RequirementSet command with its ExecutionList prerequisites.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing ExecutionList and ExecutionEntry links
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Expecting to link an ExecutionList directly to one Requirement for granular tracking.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: A list links to a RequirementSet; an entry can link its TestCase to an individual Requirement. Do not infer either link from list creation alone.

examPitfalls.title: Always dragging the entire TestSheet onto a Requirement
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Dragging the full TestSheet even when only a subset of its Instances (e.g. this sprint's) are actually in scope.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: When only some Instances belong to the current scope, select and drag just those individual Instances rather than the whole TestSheet.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester drags Instances from a TestSheet onto a Requirement before any physical TestCase has been built. What kind of link is created?
practiceQuiz.hint: This link is a planning placeholder, not the real thing yet.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The linked design Instance creates a substitute for planned coverage; it does not establish an executable TestCase or a successful execution.

optionExplanations.A: A physical TestCase link requires linking the real test; design data alone creates a substitute.
optionExplanations.B: The substitute represents the linked Instance before the physical test is linked.
optionExplanations.C: This operation links design data to a Requirement, not an ExecutionList to a set.
optionExplanations.D: A Class reference reuses design structure; it is not a Requirement coverage link.

practiceQuiz.scenario: You drag an ExecutionList itself to establish execution coverage for a group of Requirements. Which object is its documented link target (distinct from dragging an individual ExecutionEntry)?
practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish the entire list from an individual execution entry.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Drag the ExecutionList to the RequirementSet. A separate ExecutionEntry operation can link a TestCase to an individual Requirement; calculation must still be current.

optionExplanations.A: An ExecutionEntry can target an individual Requirement; the question asks about the list itself.
optionExplanations.B: The list contains execution entries referencing tests, but this is not the Requirement coverage target.
optionExplanations.C: The documented direct link is ExecutionList to RequirementSet.
optionExplanations.D: An Instance is design data, not the target for linking the list to Requirements.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Only 4 of a TestSheet's 12 Instances are planned for the current sprint. What is the correct way to link them to their Requirement?

options.text: Drag the entire TestSheet onto the Requirement, since partial linking isn't possible.
Select and drag only the 4 relevant Instances onto the Requirement.
Wait until all 12 Instances are ready before linking any of them.
Duplicate the TestSheet and delete the other 8 Instances first.

practiceQuiz.hint: Drag-and-drop linking works at the Instance level, not only the whole-TestSheet level.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Individual Instances can be selected and dragged onto a Requirement when only a subset is currently in scope — there's no need to link the whole TestSheet or wait for every Instance to be ready.

optionExplanations.A: The whole sheet would also link the eight out-of-scope Instances; selected linking is supported.
optionExplanations.B: Selecting the four Instances links only the planned scope without changing the source sheet.
optionExplanations.C: Individual Instances can be linked before the remaining eight are ready.
optionExplanations.D: Copying and deleting data is unnecessary; the operation accepts selected Instances.

quickRecap.value: Drag Instances (or the whole TestSheet) from TestCase Design onto the matching Requirement.
Placeholder link, created before the physical TestCase exists.
Replace explicitly by dragging a TestCase onto its substitute, or use Replace Substitutes by Testcases with the documented ExecutionList links.
Keep each Requirement traceable; the documented linking scopes include a TestSheet, Class or selected Instances.
Explicitly link lists to sets; entries can link individual Requirements. Recalculate outdated dashboard values.
